served: nystagmus: direction and whether it changes with gaze
results: 1. nystagmus: direction and whether it changes with gaze: ipsilesional torsional nystagmus
2. skew deviation / alternating cover test: skew deviation with LATERAL ALTERNATION - right eye hypotropic, left eye hypertropic
3. ocular torsion and head tilt: RIGHT-sided head tilt; right eye excyclotorted and left eye incyclotorted - the complete ocular tilt reaction
4. MRI brain with DWI: LEFT rostral pontine infarct and a caudal mesencephalic infarct extending along the paramedian line to the midline
5. CT / MR angiography (posterior circulation): TOP-OF-THE-BASILAR OCCLUSION; thrombectomy was deferred as he was well preserved
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Acute top-of-the-basilar ischemic syndrome due to basilar artery occlusion, causing left rostral pontine and caudal paramedian midbrain infarction with a complete ocular tilt reaction and alternating skew deviation.
Alternative: Acute vertebrobasilar embolic brainstem infarction from another posterior-circulation source.
Alternative: Central vestibular syndrome from a small cerebellar or brainstem infarct not fully visualized on MRI.
Alternative: Peripheral vestibulopathy such as vestibular neuritis.
